definitions.gloss: earthen or concrete floor at a Japanese entrance
definitions.explanation: The hard-floored lower area at the entrance of a Japanese house (genkan) where shoes are removed. Originally made by pounding a mixture of earth, lime, and bittern, now typically concrete or tile.

examples.japanese: {三和土|たたき}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ→靴を脱ぐ：23571_kutsuwonugu⟧。
examples.english: To take off shoes on the entrance floor.

examples.japanese: {三和土|たたき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{汚|よご}れていた→汚れる：01293_yogoreru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{掃除|そうじ}→掃除：02889_souji⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The entrance floor was dirty, so I cleaned it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{民家|みんか}→民家：13217_minka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{三和土|たたき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{土|つち}→土：02229_tsuchi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{固|かた}めて→固める：01929_katameru⟧⟦{作|つく}られている→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: The entrance floors of old traditional houses are made of compacted earth.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The word {三和土|たたき} comes from the process of making the floor: three materials (⟦{土|つち}→土：02229_tsuchi⟧, ⟦{石灰|せっかい}→石灰：25494_sekkai⟧, and にがり) were mixed and pounded (たたく) to create a hard surface. The kanji {三和土|さんわど} literally means "three-mixed earth."

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {三和土|たたき} is the lowest level of the ⟦{玄関|げんかん}→玄関：05003_genkan⟧ (entrance). Visitors step up from the {三和土|たたき} onto the raised floor (⟦{上|あ}がり{框|がまち}→上がり框：10774_agarigamachi⟧) when entering the house. In modern homes, the {三和土|たたき} is usually tiled or made of concrete.

USAGE:
Not to be confused with たたき as in ⟦{鰹|かつお}→鰹：06106_katsuo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧たたき (seared bonito), which is a different word.
